LLM Dojo · Ljubljana · 1 October 2026

Jev Radar Atlas

This page collects the public projects built with TypeSafe's Jev that we could find on jevradar.com, madewithjev.com and thirteen community awesome-lists, merged into 3,404 distinct projects. Jev itself labelled each one with the job it does, the field it is in and what it replaces. Together the labels show what kinds of tasks people use a decision model for.

bird's-eye view

What Jev is used for

The labels are Jev's own answers to three choice questions and two yes/no questions per project, one request each, $0.16 for all of them. A hand check of 24 random projects agreed on the job for 21. The field label leans towards "games" for playful demos, and the source texts are short, so read the shares as a rough map.

    examples

    Ten notable projects for each job

    Picked by hand from the projects that Jev rated as most unusual for a general audience, leaving out duplicates and claims that could not be checked. Each description summarises what the authors report.

    Sources: jevradar.com (crawled 22–29 September), madewithjev.com builds and community pages, and the awesome-lists by hellogumbo, yibie, walidboulanouar, lzq-0529, aaddrick, kraayenjon, AbdelStark, cobanov, v-modal, AnotiaWang, Anil-matcha, ckaraca and onmyway133, re-fetched 1 October 2026. 4,028 records were merged on GitHub repo, X post, YouTube id and URL; this page shows the 3,404 that are projects (articles, videos and official pages are left out). Cost and latency are what authors reported, in mixed units (per call, per step, per run), so the charts show spread, not a benchmark. Stars are as listed by the aggregators.
